sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Superior?
sections.html:
You can list the house with an agent, sell it yourself, or sell it as-is for cash. The choice usually comes down to repairs, timing and how much of the sale price you need to keep.

In a cold climate, a buyer's inspector looks first at the roof, siding and heating system. A listing can bring a higher price if you finish that work first. A cash sale suits owners who inherited a house, live out of town, or cannot fund roof, siding or heating repairs. Weigh what you would net on each route after repairs, taxes and the months of carrying costs.

  • Listing: more buyers, more steps, and a wait for the buyer's lender and inspection.
  • For sale by owner: you set the price and take on the paperwork, including the condition report.
  • Cash buyer: an as-is price and a closing date you agree on in writing.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Superior housing?
sections.html:
Superior is a mostly owner-occupied Wisconsin city. The Census median value for an owner-occupied home is $180,400, and 60.6 percent of housing units are owner-occupied. The 2025 population estimate of 26,397 is 1.3 percent below the 2020 base.

Nearly 18 percent of residents are 65 or older. The median is a citywide yardstick, and your own house will land above or below it depending on condition and location.

sections.h2: What makes Superior different from other Wisconsin cities?
sections.html:
Superior is the Douglas County seat, at the western tip of Lake Superior, and it forms the Twin Ports with Duluth, Minnesota. The city is bordered by Saint Louis, Superior and Allouez bays and sits between the Nemadji and Saint Louis rivers. It covers about 55.65 square miles in all, and 18.69 of those are water.

The first log cabin went up on the Nemadji in 1853, and the city was incorporated on March 25, 1889. A railroad boom from 1888 to 1892 produced the business blocks along Tower Avenue and Fairlawn Mansion, built in 1891. The port of Duluth-Superior is the largest on the Great Lakes, BNSF Railway runs an operations hub in the city, and a refinery operates here. Census figures show $415.3 million in transportation and warehousing receipts in 2022.

Census figures add detail: 85.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, households average 2.15 people, and the mean commute is 16.1 minutes. Retail sales reached $771.2 million in 2022 and health care and social assistance receipts $188.7 million. About 88.9 percent of residents are white alone and 1.4 percent are American Indian and Alaska Native alone.

The Superior School District runs one high school, one middle school and five elementary schools. The University of Wisconsin-Superior and Northwood Technical College are in the city. U.S. 2, U.S. 53, Highway 35 on Tower Avenue and Highway 105 serve the city, the John Blatnik Bridge (Interstate 535) leads to Duluth, and the Duluth Transit Authority runs city buses.

sections.h2: How does Lake Superior weather affect a Superior house?
sections.html:
Winters are severe. The 1991 to 2020 normals show a January average low of 5.8 degrees, a record low of minus 38, and 56 inches of snow a year, with 31.45 inches of total precipitation.

Heat loss, ice and snow load are the first things an inspector checks. Gather furnace service tickets, insulation work and any roof or siding invoices. Superior's property standards require heating equipment that holds 68 degrees in habitable rooms and a water heater that supplies 120-degree water at sinks, tubs and showers, so confirm both work before an appraiser or inspector visits.

sections.h2: Which Superior city code items should I fix before selling?
sections.html:
The city's building inspection office publishes a list of the most commonly violated regulations. It is written for rental owners, but most items also apply to one- and two-family homes that owners live in. Check these before you list.

  • Address numbers readable from the street day and night.
  • A tight roof with no missing or badly worn shingles, and siding in sound, weathertight condition.
  • Stairs, porches and decks in sound repair, with graspable handrails on stairs of more than three risers.
  • Smoke alarms in each sleeping room, the access area and on each story and in the basement, plus carbon monoxide alarms where state law requires them.
  • Locks on every window within 8 feet of grade.
  • Downspouts and roof drains that connect to the city sanitary sewer must be disconnected and run outside. Contact the Environmental Services Division at 715-394-5826.

Lead-safe work practices are required when painted surfaces are disturbed. Call Building Inspection at 715-395-7288 to ask which permits are on file. The city also runs an online records search covering permits, building inspections and code compliance cases from June 2021 forward.

sections.h2: What do I disclose, pay and record when I sell in Douglas County?
sections.html:
Under Chapter 709, an owner who sells a one-to-four unit property gives the buyer a completed condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. If it arrives late, the buyer has 2 business days after the 10 days to rescind. The owner may substitute written information from a licensed engineer, surveyor, pest control operator, qualified third party or contractor for any entry in that contractor's field.

The state transfer fee is 30 cents per $100, owed by the seller under section 77.22. At the Superior median value of $180,400 it comes to $541.20. Local governments may not charge their own fee on a conveyance that the state fee exempts.

The Douglas County Register of Deeds is at 1313 Belknap Street, Room 108, Superior, and can be reached at 715-395-1463. The county's 2026 fee schedule lists a $30 Register of Deeds recording fee. After a deed is recorded, check with the Real Property Lister that the tax records picked up the right owner and legal description.

sections.h2: How do Douglas County property taxes affect a Superior sale?
sections.html:
Property tax bills come from the city treasurer in mid to late December. The first installment, or full payment, is due January 31, and the second installment is due July 31. If the January 31 payment is missed, the July option is lost and interest of 1 percent per month runs on the entire balance beginning February 1.

The Lottery and Gaming Credit goes only to a primary residence, so rental or other properties do not qualify. Delinquent taxes matter before a sale. State law lets the county take a tax deed after two years, and the county says it currently uses a four-year cycle that could change. Ask the Douglas County Treasurer for a payoff figure if you owe back taxes.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Superior house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, and a listing buyer can negotiate repairs. Ask Building Inspection at 715-395-7288 whether any notice is open on the address, and answer the condition report honestly about known defects.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee on a Superior home sale?
faqs.a: The state fee is 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller. A $180,000 sale carries a $540 fee. The Douglas County Register of Deeds collects it at recording, with an electronic transfer return filed first.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Douglas County?
faqs.a: The county's 2026 fee schedule lists a $30 Register of Deeds recording fee. The transfer fee is separate. Call the Register of Deeds at 715-395-1463 to confirm the total before you send documents.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Superior?
faqs.a: The first installment or full payment is due January 31, and the second installment is due July 31. Missing the first deadline starts interest at 1 percent per month on the whole balance from February 1.

faqs.q: Does the seller owe the buyer a condition report in Superior?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Wisconsin Chapter 709 requires the owner to deliver it within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A late delivery lets the buyer rescind within 2 business days after that period. Personal representatives and trustees who never lived in the house are excused.
